summary: Discovery focused on security posture requirements for evaluating Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Major topics: SOC2/ISO requirements, SSO/SAML and Okta integration, RBAC scoping, audit logs and log retention, envelope encryption/KMS options, and data residency/retention policy. Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private due to regulated data, requested SOC2 artifacts, network diagrams, and an ops runbook for onboarding.

Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-21
Time: 14:30 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Nair (Cascade CISO), Tom Reynolds (Head of IT), Aisha Khan (DevOps), Marcus Lee (PM)

Auto-generated summary: Security posture discovery; customer has regulated genomics data and needs SOC2 + VPC/on-prem considerations.

-----
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood. Quick intro, Luis is our solutions engineer, we'll run through security posture and then dig into anything specific to your compliance.
00:18 Tom Reynolds: Hi Maya, thanks. We booked this to understand the differences between hosted, dedicated and private, and what's required from our side for networking and controls.
00:30 Maya Chen: Great. Dr. Nair, could you kick us off with your top-line compliance constraints?
00:35 Dr. Priya Nair: Sure. We're Cascade Biotech, we handle patient-derived genomics data, so PHI adjacent; need SOC 2 Type II at minimum, ISO 27001 would be nice. We also need SSO via Okta, RBAC to restrict model access, and audit logs exported to our SIEM. Data residency in us-west for the time being. Also, encryption keys must be customer-managed when possible.
00:58 Luis Ortega: Got it. When you say customer-managed keys, do you mean KMS in your cloud, or an HSM?
01:03 Dr. Priya Nair: Preferably KMS with our key policies in AWS KMS, but we might require HSM for certain projects.
01:11 Luis Ortega: Makes sense. Redwood supports both KMS integration for our hosted and dedicated setups, and for Private we can do HSM integrations depending on the deployment. There's a bit of nuance around private control plane access.
01:26 Marcus Lee: Quick Q on SOC2 — do you run SOC audits annually or do you provide the report to customers?
01:33 Maya Chen: We have SOC 2 Type II and can share the report under NDA. I'll attach the report and ISO docs after the call.
01:39 Aisha Khan: Also curious about audit log granularity — we need per-request token-level logs, not just aggregate metrics.
01:46 Luis Ortega: We capture per-request metadata and can stream audit logs to your SIEM via secure S3 or syslog push depending on your infra. There's a config for retention and export.
01:56 Tom Reynolds: What's the default retention? We can't keep data forever.
02:00 Luis Ortega: Default log retention on hosted is 90 days, you can configure longer retention with dedicated or private. For Private, retention is totally under your control; we can support your policies.
02:10 Dr. Priya Nair: Good. On SSO, we use Okta and expect SCIM + SAML for provisioning and login. Any gaps?
02:18 Maya Chen: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. There might be some minor differences in attribute mapping depending on your IdP; Luis will share a SAML metadata example and SCIM mapping doc.
02:28 Luis Ortega: Yep, we'll share step-by-step Okta setup. Also note in Dedicated you can have SSO integrated with our control plane so your users can access the console; for Private you manage the entire control plane and integrate directly.
02:42 Marcus Lee: What's the tenant isolation model? We need strong multi-tenancy separation between internal projects.
02:47 Luis Ortega: For Hosted we have logical tenant isolation — multi-tenant with strict namespace separation and encryption per-customer. For Dedicated you get isolated GPU pools and network isolation; for Private you get full isolation since it's your VPC or on-prem. The RBAC model is role-based with support for custom roles and allowed actions.
03:05 Dr. Priya Nair: Can we get admin-level audit logs and token-revocation events?
03:10 Luis Ortega: Yes, audit events include token issuance/revocation, config changes, model deployments, and access attempts. Some event names in our old transcript exports got munged — but the logs themselves contain the metadata you need.
03:21 Tom Reynolds: Network wise, how do we do peering? VPC peering or private link?
03:25 Luis Ortega: We support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (or equivalent), and for on-prem we can set up a VPN or direct connect approach. We'll provide a network diagram and sample Terraform.
03:36 Aisha Khan: Do you support egress restrictions? We need to restrict outbound connections from model containers.
03:41 Luis Ortega: Yes, in Dedicated/Private you control egress via network policies; hosted has restricted egress but some managed service endpoints are required for metrics and updates.
03:52 Marcus Lee: Any customers with similar regulated data you can reference?
03:56 Maya Chen: We have several health and biotech customers (we can provide anonymized references). I'll include a short one-pager.
04:05 Dr. Priya Nair: Encryption at rest — if we bring our KMS keys, does Redwood rewrap the model artifacts or do you store them encrypted under our key?
04:13 Luis Ortega: We use envelope encryption; for hosted/dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS to wrap the root key. For Private, since it's in your environment, you control full key lifecycle. There might be some admin-level key handling for certain managed features; we'll document those in the runbook.
04:30 Tom Reynolds: How are keys rotated? Is there an automated rotation policy?
04:34 Luis Ortega: You can supply rotation schedules via KMS; for hosted we rotate our service keys regularly and you control customer-managed key rotations. We'll show the KMS integration path.
04:45 Aisha Khan: Regarding data at rest inside the model runtime — any caching like KV cache storing prefixes? How long is that kept?
04:53 Luis Ortega: Good callout. Our runtime uses KV caches to speed generation; for hosted we have configurable TTLs and we can disable persistent caching for sensitive workloads. For Dedicated/Private you can fully control cache behavior. Some earlier docs mis-typed KV cache as K-V cash in the transcript, so we'll make sure it's clear.
05:12 Marcus Lee: Will there be any PII in logs?
05:15 Maya Chen: We try to avoid including full request payloads in logs; audit logs contain metadata and IDs. If you need full payload logs for debugging, we can set up a secure, time-limited mechanism but by default we avoid writing PHI to logs.
05:28 Dr. Priya Nair: What's your incident response and SLA on breaches?
05:33 Maya Chen: We have an incident response playbook and will notify customers per our SLA. For Dedicated/Private we support faster notification options. I'll attach our security whitepaper and IR playbook summary.
05:44 Tom Reynolds: On the legal side, we need a DPA and data processing addendum. Do you have a standard DPA?
05:49 Maya Chen: Yes, we have a standard DPA and can negotiate clauses for data residency and processing scope.
05:54 Luis Ortega: (interject) For procurement they usually ask for sub-processors list — we can provide that redacted list as well.
06:02 Marcus Lee: Can we run a perf baseline with a synthetic dataset before production?
06:07 Luis Ortega: Absolutely. For Dedicated we can reserve capacity for benchmarking. For hosted we can run a benchmark but it's shared infra so results vary; we'll plan a dedicated perf run for more deterministic numbers.
06:20 Aisha Khan: Back to SAML — we need user group sync for role mapping. Does Redwood map Okta groups to RBAC roles?
06:27 Luis Ortega: Yes, group-to-role mapping via SCIM or attribute mapping in SAML. We'll include examples.
06:36 Dr. Priya Nair: What about change control for model updates — if Redwood rolls a new runtime, how much notice?
06:42 Maya Chen: We provide release notes and for Dedicated we can do canary windows or freeze windows as part of the contract. For Private you control the upgrade schedule.
06:50 Tom Reynolds: Are there encryption attestations or pen tests we can see?
06:55 Maya Chen: We have pen test summaries and can share a redacted report under NDA.
07:02 Marcus Lee: Any constraints for air-gapped on-prem? We might need that for a future project.
07:07 Luis Ortega: We offer an on-prem package that can run air-gapped. There are extra operational requirements (airgap install scripts, periodic offline updates). We'll share the ops checklist.
07:20 Aisha Khan: For audit log export, do you offer streaming to Splunk/Datadog?
07:25 Luis Ortega: Yes, we support streaming to Splunk via HTTP Event Collector, Datadog intake, or S3 buckets.
07:32 Dr. Priya Nair: Can logs be PII-scrubbed before export?
07:36 Luis Ortega: We have hooks to redact tokens and sensitive fields; we can tailor the scrubber rules.
07:44 Tom Reynolds: What about least-privilege access — can we restrict model-publish to a small group?
07:48 Luis Ortega: Yes, we have granular permissions for publish, deploy, and config. Custom roles can be defined per-project.
07:56 Maya Chen: Ok I'm going to summarize next steps: I'll send SOC2 and ISO artifacts; Luis will send VPC diagram and Okta SCIM/SAML examples; we'll align on a pilot scope (bench + security review). Anything else?
08:09 Dr. Priya Nair: Please include the backup/retention details for model artifacts — how long are model checkpoints stored?
08:15 Luis Ortega: Model artifact retention varies by deployment; for hosted it's subject to our retention policy but we can arrange locked retention periods for Dedicated. Private it's under your control. We'll include specifics in the doc.
08:28 Marcus Lee: Can you include estimated cost delta between hosted vs dedicated for our throughput?
08:33 Maya Chen: We'll include a pro forma estimate and guidance on batching and quantization to reduce cost.
08:40 Aisha Khan: Any gotchas on bringing custom models?
08:44 Luis Ortega: We support custom model onboarding; depending on model size and architecture we may need optimization work and quantization; for private you can push models directly.
08:56 Tom Reynolds: Ok great. What's the timeline if we wanted Dedicated?
09:00 Maya Chen: Typically provisioning is 4-6 weeks after contract and network setup; pilot can start faster.
09:08 Dr. Priya Nair: For pilot we want to validate audit logs, SSO, and KMS integration.
09:12 Maya Chen: That's fair. We'll treat those as pilot acceptance criteria.
09:18 Marcus Lee: Are there any references of other biotech customers who did Dedicated?
09:22 Maya Chen: Yes, will include anonymized references.
09:27 (brief cross talk / laughter)
09:31 Maya Chen: Alright we'll wrap — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule the pilot planning meeting.
